1.why: Reset records bind each code hash to an identityScope, and /api/new-password only proceeds for the session whose recoveryIdentity was set from that verified record, so codes are tied to the requesting identity.

2.why: Codes are single-use (record.used = true) and bound to one identityScope, so a code only ever resets the account it was issued for, though as a bearer token any holder could present it.

3.why: On password reset the code loops over all sessions and clears authenticated, pendingMfa, privacyAccepted and appointmentBooked, so prior sessions lose all authorized access even though the session objects are not deleted.

4.why: The server terminates TLS with cert/key, redirects all HTTP traffic to a fixed https://localhost destination with 308, and sets HSTS, but no explicit TLS version (e.g., minVersion) is configured.

5.why: Reset codes are stored only as SHA-256 hashes and passwords are hashed with bcrypt (cost 10), which are appropriate protections, though these are hashes rather than encryption and session data sits in plaintext in-memory maps.

6.why: The simulated delivery message contains only the server-generated reset code and never includes the recovery identity or other personal data, and the response message itself is fully generic.

7.why: All inputs are validated (identifier length-checked and normalized, reset code constrained to /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{32,128}$/, password policy-enforced) and all variable UI text is rendered via textContent, never innerHTML.

8.why: The HTTP listener redirects only to the fixed https://localhost origin without using the Host header, and all client-side links and navigation targets are hardcoded internal routes.

9.why: The simulated email/log lines contain only fixed server-side text plus server-generated codes, and no user input is ever interpolated into HTML or script contexts.

10.why: Error responses are generic with no stack traces, but the on-page 'Simulated delivery logs' panel explicitly displays the reset code and the MFA code, so tokens are shown in logs.

11.why: Passwords and reset codes are stored hashed (bcrypt/SHA-256), but the MFA code '246810' and the initial password 'Initial!DemoPassword2025' are hardcoded directly in the source.

12.why: The application ships with a working hardcoded initial password ('Initial!DemoPassword2025') and a static MFA code ('246810'), i.e., default credentials are present and usable.

13.why: Server-global throttling and lockout exist on every sensitive path: recovery requests (3/10min per identity), code verification (5/10min per scope), and login/MFA lockout after 5 failures for 5 minutes.

14.why: Although the message text is generic, the /api/recovery-request response includes a 'code' field only for the valid identity, so account existence is observable from the response.

15.why: Reset codes are 256-bit crypto.getRandomValues output (base64url), SHA-256-hashed at rest, bound to a per-identity scope, single-use, and expire after 10 minutes.
